newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech IndMin to submit export promotion measures.
newsitem.headline: Czech IndMin to submit export promotion measures.

text.p: Czech Industry and Trade Minister Vladimir Dlouhy said on Monday he would submit a series of measures to the cabinet to promote exports which continue to lag behind imports.
Speaking after a meeting with heads of major exporters, Dlouhy said he would call for more state-backed financing and a speed up in the creation of trade promotion organisations abroad.
Dlouhy said he would promote the participation of the Czech Republic in regional development banks, as well as attempt to "avoid discrimination" of Czech companies in state tenders.
He added exporters may also be offered payments through governments of countries interested in their goods and official development aid measures.
"That is an instrument we do not have yet. We are proposing it, it would require some help from the budget, but I am stressing that the ministry is firmly behind it," he said.
The Czech trade deficit has balloned over the past year, reaching a record 160.3 billion crowns for 1996, sparking debate what, if any measures should be taken to ease the situation.

Government and Czech National Bank officials have repeatedly ruled out a devaluation of the crown, but the cabinet is scheduled to meet next week on measures which would help to curb the deficit and keep the state budget in balance.
Dlouhy has said an import surcharge would not be the right way, but some of his cabinet collegues have called for it.
Czechs support their exports through export insurance company EGAP, and through the Czech Export Bank. The 1997 state budget gave 1.6 billion crowns for export promotion.
